subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the supported trust lifecycle for outbound-staged generated HTML host-read delivery?
rationale: The implementation appears sound and fail-closed, but it intentionally expands a local HTML host-read boundary and adds persisted trust metadata, which automation should not approve without owner intent.

options.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
options.body: After the branch is cleanly rebased, accept the sha256+size SQLite provenance lifecycle as the narrow trust boundary for staged generated HTML.

options.title: Require A Narrower Lifecycle
options.body: Ask for a smaller or different trust mechanism before merge if persistent outbound provenance is not an acceptable security boundary.

options.title: Keep Staged HTML Blocked
options.body: Pause or close the PR if maintainers prefer to leave generated HTML fail-closed after outbound staging.

recommendation.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
recommendation.body: After the branch is cleanly rebased, accept the sha256+size SQLite provenance lifecycle as the narrow trust boundary for staged generated HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the trusted generated HTML host-read behavior that this PR extends and has the strongest feature-history signal for the trust-boundary decision.
